patch.value: GH-1549: fence item commits after an expired mutation lease is taken over

A newly received GitHub report demonstrates a stale SDK mutateItem callback silently overwriting a newer committed CLI update after TTL takeover. Independently reproduced through the public SDK entrypoint on current744a4c95a in a disposable non-Git tracker, with only locks.ttl_seconds changed to1. The peer commits successfully, the stale SDK writer is not refused, and the final title is Stale overwrite. This is small-N correctness, separate from large-N lock throughput and checkpoint claim-generation fencing.

Deterministic cross-process and same-process controls preserve a newer write after lease takeover; Stale commits return a typed conflict with bounded ownership/generation evidence and no item/history write; Preserve dead-owner recovery and explicit stale-lock policy without unsafe force advice; Audit other SDK mutation paths and document the lease/fencing contract

After another writer takes over and commits, the stale mutation refuses before overwriting item or authoritative history state; the newer committed value remains unchanged. Preserve supported stale takeover and proven-dead-owner recovery policies.

Isolated public-SDK plus CLI reproduction: ttl1, newerCommitted=true, staleWriterRefused=false, finalTitle=Stale overwrite. Current source remains affected; no production tracker was used or modified.
